title: Undo drawer: Even-key census
summary: A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
An experimental filing machine records both new cards and requests to undo recent cards. Mina separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement undoDrawerEvenKeyCensus(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Stack history. A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with stack history. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

A nonnegative event pushes that value onto a stack. A negative event removes up to abs(event) values from its top. Produce the final stack from bottom to top. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,0,12]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 2.
The derived sequence is [4]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 1.
The derived sequence is []. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 0.
